---
title: "How do I display the distribution of numerical observations?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I display the distribution of numerical observations?

## Steps to decide and solve

Check that the variable is numeric; choose sensible bins and units; display counts and use mean/median reference lines only when useful.

## Worked example: faithful

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("faithful")
h <- ru_apply("histogram", data=d, x="eruptions")
stopifnot(sum(h$counts)==nrow(d))
```

Geyser eruption durations are clustered, so the histogram reveals features that a single mean conceals. Bar height measures the count of observations in each interval, not the probability of an exact duration.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("histogram", data=your_data, x="numeric_column")
```

If the question asks for counts by distinct labels rather than numerical intervals, select bar_chart. If it asks to compare groups, use grouped_boxplot or comparable histograms.

Use `ru_plan("histogram")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
